stem: Affected plants are all from one propagation batch while adjacent older plants under the same room conditions are normal. How should this pattern influence the differential?
choices: Increase attention to batch-specific propagation history, root condition, source health, and handling while still testing shared room factors against matched unaffected plants.
Treat the normal older plants as evidence that the room environment can be excluded from the differential for the affected batch.
Treat the batch pattern as presumptive evidence of a transmissible propagation problem and begin containment while other causes are investigated.
Adjust the room environment toward the needs of the affected batch because the normal older plants are already acclimated and may not reveal the same stress.
rationale: A batch-limited pattern is valuable because it raises the probability of cohort-specific explanations such as propagation stress, root quality, source-plant health, handling, or batch-specific exposure. It does not eliminate the environment, since younger or recently propagated plants may respond differently to the same room conditions. It also does not prove a pathogen. The strongest workup therefore uses the batch pattern to reprioritize hypotheses while comparing matched unaffected plants and shared environmental evidence.
